title: Lite Assistant Modules — lab journal
body:
Purpose / elevator: sketching a modular, tiny-footprint assistant runtime made of independent capability modules (skills) that can be composed at runtime by higher-level orchestration. Target: low-latency endpoints and constrained dedicated pools (edge + mobile + tiny-hosted lanes).

Quick notes to self:
- Not trying to replace full assistant surface — goal is deterministic, auditable, cheap building blocks: intent-extract, slot-fill, fact-lookup, summarizer-lite, safe-rewriter.
- Modules should be small models or distilled policy wrappers + simple state schemas.
- Primary constraints: 50ms median p95 < 250ms, memory < 1GB per module on lite node.

User problems we're solving:
- Product teams want predictable cost lanes for trivial assistant tasks (e.g., field-level autofill, short summaries, attribute extraction) without invoking multi-GPU models.
- Operations want composability so we can A/B a single module without touching the whole assistant.
- Security/compliance teams want module-level E2E logging and per-module KMS scoping.

High-level architecture (sketch):
- Module descriptor: name, input schema, output schema, cost profile, fallback chain, model artifact id (quantized variant), privacy flags.
- Runtime "module runtime" that loads modules lazily; lightweight IPC between router and module; per-module cache (prefix + kv).
- Orchestrator (hosted) maps a request to a module graph (1..N modules), routes to cheapest compatible zone (edge/dedicated) with fallback.
- Telemetry: token count per module, latency per module, correctness score from eval hooks (sampled).

Example module catalog entries (proto):
- intent-lite-v1: small classifier (2-4M params distill), input: text, output: intent id + confidence. Accepts short contexts. Expected latencies 30–80ms on lite-host.
- slot-fill-smol: fills up to 6 slots from prompt + structured hints, best-effort coreference, returns canonicalized fields.
- summarizer-compact: extractive summarizer tuned for 40–80 token outputs.

User stories (rough):
- As a product engineer, I want to swap the slot-fill module with a higher-precision variant during canary so my feature can test without changing routing code.
- As an SRE, I want per-module quotas and circuit-breaker so a noisy module can't exhaust the lite pool.
- As a compliance reviewer, I want module-level audit trail and a flag to disable modules that persist PII.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Module descriptor + registry implemented, docs for creating a module (YAML + model artifact), internal CLI to publish to catalog.
- Runtime can load 3 module types concurrently on a lite-host with < 800MB total memory.
- Routing policy can select cheapest compatible region and fall back to hosted full-assistant if module fails.
- Basic telemetry: per-module 95th latency, error rate, and token count emitted to Console.

Experiments to run (early):
- Bench: run intent-lite-v1 and summarizer-compact on t4-small and on an arm-based edge instance. Capture median/p95 and memory.
- Quality trade-off: A/B distill sizes (2M vs 8M params) to see delta in accuracy vs latency.
- Cost sim: synthetic workload of 10k requests/day — estimate cost per 1k requests for module lane vs full assistant lane.

Open questions / risks:
- How do we compose module outputs cleanly? e.g., slot-fill depends on intent; we need a lightweight schema and simple error propagation rules.
- State passing: temporary vs persistent. Do we allow modules to store short-lived context with TTL or require orchestrator-managed state?
- Security: modules may call external lookups (KBs). Need module-level KMS tokens and per-module egress controls.
- Versioning: if a module descriptor changes schema, how to do graceful rollouts? need explicit transformation adapters.

Metrics targets (draft):
- Latency: median < 60ms, p95 < 300ms for single-module calls on lite-host pool.
- Cost: target < 15% of equivalent-hosted full-assistant cost for common micro-tasks.
- Accuracy: module-specific evals should not regress >2% vs baseline for production-tagged modules.

Telemetry / eval hooks:
- Small eval harness that runs N prompt sets (sampled from prod) every 24h against module variants and reports drift (precision/recall / summary ROUGE-lite).
- Telemetry must tag which module variant and which host (edge/dedicated/hosted).

UX notes (product):
- Console: module catalog UI, quick-preview for each module (input example -> sample output), "compose" UI to define a tiny DAG of modules for a route.
- SDK: lightweight client to call a single module or a module graph. Simplify developer surface: modules.call("intent-lite-v1", {text:...}) or modules.graph("checkout-flow-v2", payload).

Rollout playbook (sketch):
1) Internal alpha: only dev teams, require opt-in flag on route.
2) Canary: route 5% of traffic through module graph in prod for one customer segment. Monitor error rate/quality.
3) Scale: expand to low-latency tier customers and add autoscale triggers for lite pools.

Next steps / TODOs (me):
- [ ] Draft registry Yaml spec (fields + schema examples). (INF-3421)
- [ ] Spin up prototype lite-host on arm-sim in perf lab and run single-module bench. (GH PR #87)
- [ ] Sketch Console UX mock: catalog list + compose flow. Invite Zara for quick whiteboard.
- [ ] Write up security checklist for module egress + KMS scoping and submit to sec review.

Notes to self / heuristics while prototyping:
- Favor deterministic transforms where possible (extract -> reformat) to reduce hallucination surface.
- For hybrid flows, prefer "call lightweight module, then full assistant for fallback" rather than chaining multiple heavy models.
- Keep module API intentionally simple: single JSON input and single JSON output (opinionated narrow schemas).

Random ideas to keep in backlog:
- Module marketplace (internal) where teams can publish tuned modules for domain-specific tasks (finance anonymizer, health-sanitizer).
- On-device tiny runtime (mobile SDK) that can host a single intent-lite for offline onboarding flows.
- Adaptive routing: start with module lane and escalate to full assistant only if confidence < threshold.
